name: 15th Wing Operations Center
description: Wing-level execution monitoring for tasked sorties.

doctrineSource.note: Wing Operations Center function is standard; the 15th Wing's specific internal C2 structure was not independently verified during this research pass.

name: Air Operations Center (AOC) Tasking Function
description: The AOC's Combat Operations Division tasking function that produces the daily ATO plus supporting SPINS/ACO.

name: Strategy Division (SRD)
description: Long-range and near-term strategy planning; develops, refines, disseminates, and assesses JFACC strategy guidance. Comprises the Strategy Plans Team, Strategy Guidance Team, and Operational Assessment Team.

name: Combat Plans Division (CPD)
description: Near-term AOC planning (within 48 hours prior to ATO execution). Comprises the Targeting Effects Team (TET), MAAP Team, ATO Production Team, and C2 Plans Team. This is the division that actually builds the ATO — not Combat Operations Division, which executes it.

name: Combat Operations Division (COD)
description: Executes the current ATO/ATONEWS and ACO during the 24-hour execution period. Comprises the Offensive Operations Team, Defensive Operations Team, Component Joint Data Network Team, and the Senior Intelligence Duty Officer (SIDO) team. Corrects an earlier ENSIM assumption that this division builds the ATO — per AFMAN 13-1AOC Vol 3, that is CPD's role; COD executes it.

name: Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance Division (ISRD)
description: Assesses and anticipates adversary activity, plans ISR operations, and develops dynamic target strategies. Comprises the Analysis, Correlation, and Fusion (ACF) Team, Targets/Tactical Assessment (TGT/TA) Team, and ISR Operations Team.

name: Air Mobility Division (AMD)
producesArtifacts: Joint Integrated Prioritized Requirements List (JIPRL) coordination
description: Plans, coordinates, tasks, and executes air mobility missions per JFACC guidance, in a process run parallel to and integrated with the main air tasking cycle. Coordinates intertheater air mobility missions directly with the 618 AOC/TACC. Comprises the Airlift Control Team, Air Refueling Control Team, Aeromedical Evacuation Control Team, and Air Mobility Control Team. This is the doctrinally correct home for DIRMOBFOR's coordination function and for Mission 1's airlift tasking, not the generic CPD/ATO path.

doctrineSource.note: Cited via the AOC-DFO corpus registry, not independently fetched in this session — treat as a lead for deeper AMD/DIRMOBFOR sourcing, not yet verified firsthand.

name: 618 AOC/TACC Mission Tasking
description: 24/7 execution node tasking specific tail numbers and crews for AMC-owned global mobility missions, even when the aircraft flying it is theater-assigned.

name: Tactical Operations Center (Light) (TOC-L)
producesArtifacts: Air picture / sensor-fusion common operating picture
description: A real, current, deployable USAF C2 kit: fuses data from hundreds of sensor/battle-management feeds into a common air picture, connects to aircraft and other C2 agencies, and is staffed by a handful of personnel versus ~100 for a full-size Control and Reporting Center (CRC). Publicly demonstrated across PACAF's Indo-Pacific AOR (Misawa, Yokota, Guam) in 2025 exercises. Its use here as the element that produces UAV flight plans and issues detailed launch instructions to the Loadmaster is this mission's own extension of TOC-L's real, more general C2/sensor-fusion role — no source found this session documents TOC-L specifically performing airdropped-UAV flight planning.

doctrineSource.publication: "Air Force TOC-L enhances joint force C2"
doctrineSource.note: Confirmed via web search on 2026-09-07 (real, current USAF program; corroborated by a second af.mil article, 'Next-gen TOC-L systems announced to boost agile C2 capabilities,' and independent defense trade press: Air & Space Forces Magazine, DefenseScoop, The Defense Post). Direct fetch of the af.mil article itself returned a network-level 403 this session — same .mil constraint noted on other records. This record's specific claim that TOC-L produces UAV flight plans for a palletized-effects airdrop is NOT from any source — it is this mission's fictional extension of TOC-L's real, documented air-battle-management/sensor-fusion function, stated explicitly rather than presented as doctrine.
